clue.text: Court that condemned murderer

indicators.note: something condemned is wrecked or ruined, so the letters of the two words are wrecked into a new order

explanation.surface: A court has passed sentence on a killer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'condemned' looks like the court's verdict on the murderer, but it is the anagram signal working on COURT THAT.
explanation.definitionFit: A cutthroat is a ruthless killer, originally one who slits throats.

clue.text: Church dignitary's first to receive honours, laid on thick

indicators.note: the church letters receive, i.e. take inside, the honours letters

parts.note: CE is the Church of England
AK is an honour, Knight of the Order of Australia

indicators.note: the first letter of the word dignitary is taken

explanation.surface: A senior cleric is the first in line for an honours award, praised lavishly.
explanation.walkthrough: AK, Knight of the Order of Australia, is a less familiar honour than the usual OBE or MBE; 'Church dignitary' tempts as one unit but splits.
explanation.definitionFit: Something caked has been plastered on in a thick coating, like mud on boots.

clue.text: Story of rupees found in tree covered by press

indicators.note: the tree letters sit between the two halves of the press phrase, covered by it

parts.note: the papers, i.e. newspapers, are the press

indicators.note: the rupee letter is found inside the tree word

parts.note: the aspen is a kind of poplar tree
R is the abbreviation for rupees, the Indian currency

explanation.surface: A newspaper tale about money discovered in a tree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'covered by' means the press phrase splits in two to wrap round the tree-with-rupee, not that one sits over the other.
explanation.definitionFit: The Aspern Papers is a novella by Henry James, so it is a story by title.

clue.text: Coward created this affliction

definitions.meaning: Noël Coward wrote a comedy of this title in 1924
a seasonal pollen allergy causing sneezing

explanation.surface: A fearful person brought on this ailment.
explanation.definitionFit: Hay Fever is a Noël Coward play, and the pollen allergy is an ailment.

clue.text: Work is nothing —- drink up!

parts.note: O, the round figure zero, means nothing

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word for drink is read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: to sup is to drink

explanation.surface: Work counts for nothing, so drink up!
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' only works because this is a down entry, read from bottom to top.
explanation.definitionFit: An opus is a creative work, especially a numbered musical composition.

clue.text: One proverbially hard job given to schoolteacher

parts.note: a task is a job
a master is a male schoolteacher in British schools

explanation.surface: A tough assignment is set by a teacher.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase 'a hard taskmaster' is the proverb the definition points to.
explanation.definitionFit: A taskmaster is a demanding overseer, and 'a hard taskmaster' is the stock phrase.

clue.text: Mystic showing unshakable faith in cosmos's origins

indicators.note: the origins of the words are their first letters, taken in turn

explanation.surface: A spiritual person displays steadfast belief in the universe.
explanation.definitionFit: Sufic means belonging to Sufism, the mystical tradition of Islam, so it describes a mystic.

clue.text: Staying home with daughter, throw noisy party

indicators.note: the home and daughter letters stay inside the throw word

parts.note: to shy is to throw, as at a coconut shy
in means at home

explanation.surface: Kept in with a daughter, someone decides to host a rowdy do.
explanation.walkthrough: A coconut shy is a British fairground stall where balls are thrown at coconuts, hence shy for throw.
explanation.definitionFit: A shindy is an informal word for a noisy party or a commotion.

clue.text: Even longer, we hear, to holiday when he'll be sacked

indicators.note: what we hear is how a word sounds when spoken, not how it is written

parts.note: farther means further, so even longer in distance
Christmas is a holiday

explanation.surface: An even longer wait for the holidays, when one man will lose his job.
explanation.walkthrough: In non-rhotic British speech FARTHER sounds like FATHER. 'Sacked' misleads: he is not fired, he carries a sack of presents.
explanation.definitionFit: Santa is pictured carrying a sack of toys, so he is a sacked figure in this playful sense.

clue.text: We attribute lane closures to work of politician

parts.note: coning is the closing of road lanes with traffic cones
in 'attribute X to Y', the to marks the author, as by does on a title page

explanation.surface: We blame the roadworks on a novel by a statesman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'We attribute' pairs with 'to': saying conings were by someone is attributing them. Coningsby is a novel by Benjamin Disraeli, a British prime minister.
explanation.definitionFit: Coningsby is an 1844 novel by Disraeli, a Victorian Prime Minister, so it is a work by a politician.

clue.text: Unlike a ruined gambler, don't panic!

definitions.meaning: a ruined gambler has lost his shirt, so the opposite still wears it
an idiomatic way of telling someone to stay calm

explanation.surface: Advice to stay calm, unlike a gambler who has lost everything.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom tells someone to calm down; literally it means not losing one's shirt as a broke gambler does.

clue.text: Duke's overcoat left out for cleaner

parts.note: D is the abbreviation for Duke

indicators.note: the letter for left is removed from the coat word

parts.note: an ulster is a long loose overcoat

explanation.surface: A nobleman's coat has been left outside for the cleaner.
explanation.walkthrough: An ulster is an old-fashioned Irish-style overcoat; 'left out' sounds like the coat abandoned outdoors.
explanation.definitionFit: A duster is a cloth used for cleaning, so it is a cleaner.

clue.text: Love to fly in alternate directions a bit

indicators.note: the fly and love letters go inside the pair of directions

parts.note: south and north, compass directions opposite one another
a midge is a small fly
love is zero in tennis, written O

explanation.surface: A lover flies to and fro, a little.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts MIDGE + O between S and N.
explanation.definitionFit: A smidgeon is a tiny amount, so a bit.

clue.text: With boldness start off fresco in style of van Gogh

indicators.note: the start of the word fresco, its first letter, is taken

parts.note: Vincent van Gogh famously cut off part of his ear, so he was without an ear
the suffix -ly turns a word into one meaning in that manner

explanation.surface: Boldly begin a wall painting in the manner of the Dutch master.
explanation.walkthrough: F comes from 'start off' fresco; van Gogh cut off his ear, and -LY means 'in the style of'.
explanation.definitionFit: Fearlessly means without fear, so with boldness.

clue.text: Go before there's pressure and advice to stop

parts.note: P is the symbol for pressure in physics
rede is an archaic word for advice
to cease is to stop

explanation.surface: Get there first, since there is pressure and counsel to halt.
explanation.definitionFit: To predecease someone is to die before them, so to go before.

clue.text: Like mistletoe to be paid for by someone else

definitions.meaning: mistletoe lives off its host tree

definitions.text: to be paid for by someone else

explanation.surface: Getting kisses under the mistletoe on someone else's tab.
explanation.definitionFit: Parasitic describes an organism or person living off a host, as mistletoe does on trees.

clue.text: Bill is victim of giant

parts.note: AC is short for account, a bill

explanation.surface: Bill is the one picked on by a big bully.
explanation.walkthrough: In Greek myth Acis was crushed by the Cyclops Polyphemus.
explanation.definitionFit: Acis, lover of Galatea, was killed by the giant Cyclops Polyphemus in Greek myth.

clue.text: Diamond, or rock, extremely obvious amid false pearls

annotationWithheld.why: Clue held as 'Diamond, or rock, extremely obvious amid false pearls': PEARLS anagram plus RK from rock's outer letters gives the answer, but 'obvious' has no job, so the clue looks misread; scan is blank and searches find nothing
annotationWithheld.clue: Diamond, or rock, extremely obvious amid false pearls

clue.text: Very undesirable position in forces

definitions.meaning: ... as an adjective means foul or offensive
a military grade such as sergeant or major

explanation.surface: A lowly place in the army.
explanation.definitionFit: Rank means foul as an adjective and a military grade as a noun.

clue.text: Are they somewhat into recycling energy?

definitions.text: Are they somewhat into recycling energy?

parts.words: Are they somewhat into recycling energy?
parts.note: a question about a group keen on reuse and clean power, read as a description of a political party

explanation.surface: A question about whether some people are keen on reusing power.
explanation.definitionFit: The ecological political party campaigns for recycling and renewable energy.

clue.text: Give way to pressure as shield finally fails

indicators.note: the final letter of the shield word fails, i.e. drops off

parts.note: a buckler is a small round shield

explanation.surface: A shield gives way under pressure at last.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finally fails' removes R, the last letter of BUCKLER.
explanation.definitionFit: To buckle is to bend or collapse under pressure, so to give way.

clue.text: By which legally countries limit workers' organisation?

definitions.text: By which legally countries limit workers' organisation?

indicators.note: the country word surrounds, and so limits, the union letters

parts.note: states are countries
TU is short for trade union

explanation.surface: Asking how governments lawfully curb trade unions.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue doubles as a description of what such laws do, so it reads as wordplay and definition at once.
explanation.definitionFit: Statutes are written laws, the means by which states legally restrict unions.

clue.text: Go wrong about a quarter of the way through sentence? Use this

indicators.note: the err letters go round the rest

parts.note: to err is to go wrong

indicators.note: a quarter of the word sentence is its first two letters of eight

explanation.surface: Advice to someone who slips up partway through writing a sentence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sentence' has eight letters, so a quarter of the way through gets two of them.
explanation.definitionFit: An eraser rubs out written mistakes, so it is the tool you use for the slip.

clue.text: Mammal is unusually alert

indicators.note: unusually means in an uncommon way, so the letters fall in an uncommon order

explanation.surface: An animal is unusually watchful.
explanation.definitionFit: The ratel, or honey badger, is an African mammal.

clue.text: Injecting heroin, drop tobacco

indicators.note: the heroin letter is injected into the drop word

parts.note: to sag is to droop or drop
H is slang for heroin

explanation.surface: A junkie lets their tobacco fall while shooting up.
explanation.definitionFit: Shag is a coarse-cut tobacco.

clue.text: The TV's unendurable? Spend what you want

parts.note: Sky is a British satellite TV broadcaster
'the limit' describes something past bearing

explanation.surface: Grumbling that television is unbearable.
explanation.walkthrough: Sky is a UK satellite television company.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means there is no upper bound, so you may spend as much as you like.

clue.text: Actors' sound place in society

indicators.note: sound here means the way a word is said, so a word heard the same is wanted

parts.note: the cast is the actors in a production

explanation.surface: Actors have a solid social standing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sound' looks like an adjective (healthy) but signals the homophone.
explanation.definitionFit: A caste is a hereditary social class, a place in society.

clue.text: Ash Wednesday at last — girls gad madly around

indicators.note: the last letter of the word Wednesday is taken
running madly around jumbles the letters into a new order

explanation.surface: On Ash Wednesday, girls finally run wild.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ash' looks like part of Ash Wednesday but is the definition alone.
explanation.definitionFit: Yggdrasil is the giant ash tree of Norse mythology binding the worlds.
